name: paywall-gate
title: Paywall gate
description: The subscribe-to-keep-reading moment: a fade over the last lines of an article, the offer, the price and a sign-in link for members.
docs: Pass the teaser (the last visible lines of the article, as real text), the headline of the offer, three benefits, the price with its period, the primary action and, for members, a sign-in link. remaining says why the reader sees the wall (You have read 3 of 3 free articles this month) and eyebrow adds a small badge with a lock. The teaser fades out with a CSS mask, which is a visual effect only: the words stay in the page for a screen reader and the card has a heading of its own, so the fade carries no information a reader would miss. Place the block directly under the visible paragraphs of the article. For search engines: a wall that shows crawlers more than readers reads as cloaking. Describe the article with JSON-LD that sets isAccessibleForFree to false and adds a hasPart whose cssSelector matches the gated part of the page (pass className="paywall" to this block, or name the wrapper of the content it hides), as Google's paywalled content guidance asks, and send crawlers the same teaser readers see. The action is a link when it has an href and a button when it has not; a function needs a client component around the block. A numeric price is written as money in the currency and locale you pass, and text such as Free is shown as written. labels translates Already a member? and Sign in.
